text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Planning Minister Khalaf says Jordan aims to cut customs duties to 30 percent next year. Sales taxes on certain items like cars will increase to compensate for cuts in duty; more items likely to be accepted free of duty, while duty on intermediate goods will be reduced.
- Crown Prince Hassan says in Washington that moving U.S. embassy from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem will not help peace.
- Ahmed Daqamsa, who shot Israeli girls in March, to be sent for psychological tests to assess his mental state.

- Cabinet to discuss shortly a new law reforming government administration which would offer government employees voluntary and provisional retirement, during which they could work for the private sector if they wished. New law would also offer longer periods of unpaid leave.
- Head of Jordan ports authority says Aqaba port will not be affected by opening of borders between Syria and Iraq. Says U.N. oil-for-food deal with Iraq involves importing goods through Aqaba.
- Jordanian energy official discusses supply of Iraqi oil to Jordan during talks in Baghdad.
- Jordanian politicians consider possibility of sending parliamentary delegation to Damascus to try to improve relations between Syria and Jordan.
- Crown Prince Hassan calls for dialogue between United States and Baghdad.
- Crown Prince Hassan says Jordan's parliamentary elections will be held on time, before the end of the year.
- Talks expected next week between planning ministry officials and World Bank on $44 million loan to develop Jordan's tourist sites of Petra, Wadi Rum and Jerash.
- U.S. to announce $100 million in additional aid to Jordan.
- Prime Minister Majali to visit United Arab Emirates, Tunisia and Egypt in the next three weeks.
